clue.text: Over a pound to 'enter contest

indicators.note: the pound sign is told to go into the word for contest, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to contest is to compete
L, from the Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A bettor puts more than a pound on a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: When a match or a meeting is finished it is said to be over, just as it is said to be done or ended.

clue.text: Indifferent type abandoning exercise may be found in hospital

parts.note: casual means offhand, indifferent

indicators.note: the word for exercise is left out of the word type

parts.note: taken as written
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: An apathetic person who gives up exercise ends up in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident victim or injured person is brought to a ward for treatment.

clue.text: Her charm a change for a tea party attendant

indicators.note: the letters of her charm a are given a change of order

explanation.surface: Her allure alters for a guest at an afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The mad tea party is the scene in Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland where this character is a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland this creature sits at the Mad Hatter's table.

clue.text: Lean over backwards to have a dance

definitions.text: Lean over backwards to have a dance

parts.words: Lean over backwards to have a dance
parts.note: the phrase suggests going out of your way, but describes a dancer bending back to pass under a low bar

explanation.surface: Going out of one's way just to get a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'lean over backwards' means try very hard; here it is literal, the posture of a Caribbean dance under a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: In this West Indian dance the dancer bends back to pass under a bar lowered each round.

clue.text: Cut in deposit renegotiated

indicators.note: the letters of deposit are worked out again into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A reduction in a down payment after fresh talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a reduction but is a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of beef from the outer thigh is a butcher's cut.

clue.text: Capital accruing initially to the partners

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word accruing is wanted here

parts.note: taken as written
North and South are partners at the bridge table, abbreviated N and S

explanation.surface: Money building up at first for the partners in a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as money in the partnership; it is the definition, a capital city. In bridge, North and South play as a pair, so 'partners' gives N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the chief city and seat of government of Greece.

clue.text: Find path from the summit, perhaps

parts.note: a track is a rough path
coming from the top is going down

explanation.surface: Locate a route off the mountain top.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace and locate something after searching is to find it.

clue.text: High flier of course

definitions.meaning: a large bird of prey soaring high
a golf score on the course, two under par on a hole

explanation.surface: A soaring bird, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally', but means on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A great bird of prey soars aloft, and in golf the same word is a score two strokes under par.

clue.text: Comes up in support of Society toffs

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits under the first, holding it up

parts.note: to well, as tears well, is to rise up

explanation.surface: Rises in backing of high society snobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffs and swells are both slang for fashionably dressed upper-class people.

clue.text: Logs made from northern trees

indicators.note: the answer is built out of the following letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Firewood cut from trees in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Logs' looks like timber but is a verb: records, writes down.
explanation.definitionFit: To log data is to record it, to put it into a record.

clue.text: Footballers' get-together

parts.note: a gathering of footballers sounds like a social meeting, but the players meant are rugby forwards packing down together

explanation.surface: Players meet up for a social evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is football too (rugby football), and its forwards bind together to restart play.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the forwards of each side lock heads and push to win the ball after a stoppage.

clue.text: Shape confined to fish

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut in
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A form kept within the limits of fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star figure is a geometric shape.

clue.text: Goddess exposing Herbert to dire trouble

parts.note: the humorist A. P. Herbert signed his Punch pieces with his initials A.P.H.

indicators.note: the words to dire are put in trouble, so their letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A goddess reveals a man called Herbert to some terrible difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: A. P. Herbert was a British writer and MP known by his initials; 'trouble' rearranges TO DIRE into RODITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek deity of love and beauty.

clue.text: Ring for a lass, it is said

indicators.note: this phrase tells the solver that the girl's name is to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Nell is a girl's name, so a lass

explanation.surface: Calling on a girl, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral bell's toll is a ring, the slow sound of a bell.

clue.text: Long walk pirates ordered

indicators.note: the letters of pirates are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Buccaneers commanded to march a great distance.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge wearily over a distance is a tiring, lengthy tramp on foot.

clue.text: Long drink containing very soft fruit

parts.note: to pine is to long for

indicators.note: the drink holds the musical mark inside it

parts.note: ale is a drink
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very soft

explanation.surface: A tall drink with some squishy fruit in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical fruit with spiky skin and sweet yellow flesh.

clue.text: Rabble's downfall

definitions.meaning: a useless lot of people, a slang term of contempt

explanation.surface: The collapse of a mob.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling a group 'a right shower' is British slang for a hopeless bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly crowd can be scorned as a bad lot, and a brief spell of rain is a fall from the sky.

clue.text: Take out girl met in: select environment

indicators.note: the girl is found inside the select circle, one piece within another

parts.note: an elite is a select group, a privileged circle
Mina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Escort a girl you met in an exclusive setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out' suggests a date with the girl but means remove.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove or get rid of something is to take it out.

clue.text: Money obtained from hobby

definitions.meaning: money earned on savings or a loan

explanation.surface: Cash gained from a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks pay a percentage on deposits, and a pastime is something that holds your attention.

clue.text: One inclined to be more than skinny

definitions.meaning: a person or thing tilting or propping itself at an angle
thinner still, the comparative of a word for thin

explanation.surface: Someone tending to be thinner than merely slim.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tilts against a wall is one who props; thinner with less fat is the comparative of slim.

clue.text: A couple of soldiers to make good

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: Two troops are sent to fix things.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers (RE) are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend or restore something is to make good the damage.

clue.text: Island's leading figure sent back home

parts.note: the Isle of Man is the island, with its possessive

indicators.note: the letters for the leading figure are turned to read backwards

parts.note: the top person is number one, written NO 1

explanation.surface: An island's chief is dispatched to his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses NO 1, giving 1 ON, read as ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A large stately house is a grand dwelling.

clue.text: Stable without a runner

indicators.note: here without means outside, the stable word goes round the a

parts.note: a manger is the feeding trough found in a stable, standing in for the stable here

explanation.surface: A stable with no racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking; and 'runner' is one who runs a business, not a horse. A manger stands in a stable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs an organisation is in charge of it.

clue.text: Bill on the line expressing agreement

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: AC is an account, a bill
a cord is a line or string

explanation.surface: A bill on the telephone line showing consent.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmony between parties, a consensus, is concord.

clue.text: Feature article on. Worcester, perhaps

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature story about the city of Worcester.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Worcester is a famous English maker of porcelain, so 'Worcester, perhaps' is an example of fine pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester ware is a type of porcelain, made in the English city.

clue.text: Gather in train ferry

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words train ferry

explanation.surface: Collect people on the train and the ferry.
explanation.definitionFit: To conclude from evidence is to deduce something.

clue.text: Drink before business — it's.no joke without it

indicators.note: the drink comes ahead of the word for business

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink
a line is a line of business, a trade

explanation.surface: Having a drink before work is no laughing matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The final sentence that delivers the laugh is what makes a funny story work.

clue.text: It sounds like a crowd in the store

indicators.note: signals that the word for a crowd is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a horde is a large crowd

explanation.surface: There's noise like a throng in the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' is a stockpile, not a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden stockpile of valuables is a cache.

clue.text: Young cricket side bound to succeed

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
to spring is to leap, to bound

explanation.surface: A junior cricket team destined to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young' as a noun means children, as in an animal and its young. The off side is the half of the cricket field facing the batter's bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Children or descendants are a parent's young.

clue.text: The byword 'of our times

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the dates of our own era
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The catchphrase of the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: A saying or proverb that everyone knows is a byword.

clue.text: Staff return by firm in southern England

indicators.note: the word for staff is turned around to read backwards

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
set means solid, firm, as a jelly sets

explanation.surface: Employees come back to a company in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees but is a stick. Dorset is a county on the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county lying in the south of England.

clue.text: Bank requires stamp in permit

indicators.note: the stamp goes inside the word for permit

parts.note: to grant is to permit or allow
a die is a tool for stamping a design

explanation.surface: A bank asks for a rubber stamp on a permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a financial institution, but it is a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank is a sloping rise of ground, a slope.
